description: Search for flights between cities and airports. Find available flights with schedules, pricing, airline information, and seat availability for domestic and international travel. Returns one page per direction: limit flights (default 7, maximum 20), chosen so that airlines and departure times (night, morning, afternoon, evening) are mixed, not only the cheapest, and listed cheapest first. total_count is how many flights the search found (total_by_route per direction on a round trip), returned_count how many are listed; when pagination.has_more is true, page 2, 3 and so on list the rest. Each flight's price_breakdown is the total for all passengers (price_scope total_for_all_passengers); average_price_breakdown is the average per adult/child passenger (price_scope per_passenger_average_excluding_infants): infant fares are excluded, so with infants it does not multiply back to the total. With more than one passenger, quote the total and say it covers all passengers. Zero price fields are left out. provider_packages are the flight's fare packages: extra_price_total is what the package adds to price_breakdown.total for all passengers and extra_price_per_passenger per passenger (0 is the fare the listed price is for), items is what the package includes (baggage, seat, meal, refund and change rights) and not_included names what it lacks. For a time of day (morning, after 18:00, ...) or a budget, send departure_after/departure_before (return_after/return_before for the return flight) or max_price instead of filtering the listed flights yourself: the filters apply to every flight of the search, so total_count and the pages count only matching flights and the search_url opens the same filtered list. Each segment's available_seats is the seat count the airline reports, which airlines cap, so the highest value means that many seats or more, not exactly that many. search_params.cabin_class is the class that was searched; location_note says which city or airport was searched when that differs from the words sent (e.g. the nearest airport of a town without one). Use this instead of fetching the site's pages when you need its prices or availability. Use when the user wants flights between two places on given dates. Dates are DD.MM.YYYY. Results include search_url, which opens the same results on the site. When the user wants specific airlines, pass their IATA codes as airlines. For the cheapest day in a period, use flight_price_calendar first and search only the chosen day here. To give a booking link for the flights the user chose, pass their enuid values to flight_allocate.

adults.description: Number of adult passengers (adults and children together at most 9)

airlines.description: Only flights with these airlines, as IATA codes (e.g., ['BA', 'TK']). Send only when the user asks for specific airlines.

cabin_class.description: Cabin class: ECONOMY, PREMIUM_ECONOMY, BUSINESS or FIRST; any other value is an error

departure_after.description: Earliest departure time of the outbound flight, HH:MM (e.g. '18:00'); omit for any time

departure_before.description: Latest departure time of the outbound flight, HH:MM (e.g. '12:00'); omit for any time

infants.description: Number of infant passengers (0-2 years, at most one per adult)

limit.description: Flights per direction per page (default 7, maximum 20)

max_price.description: Highest price per passenger (average_price_breakdown, search currency) for each direction; omit for any price

page.description: Page number from 1 (default 1); page 2, 3 … continue the same search

return_after.description: Earliest departure time of the return flight, HH:MM; only with return_date

return_before.description: Latest departure time of the return flight, HH:MM; only with return_date

name: flight_search
title: Search flights
